li.label: touch-averse
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} is uncomfortable being touched by people {PAWN_pronoun} does not already trust. Romance waits until {PAWN_pronoun} is fine with that person's touch — standing across the room is not enough. Crowding and sharing a bed with anyone else is draining.

li.label: reserved
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} likes a little space. {PAWN_pronoun} will not start a romance until {PAWN_pronoun} is at ease near that person. A trusted friend standing close is fine; strangers in touching distance are not.

li.label: touch-intolerant
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} cannot stand being touched by anyone {PAWN_pronoun} is not already intimate with. Romance only happens after a long close trust. Crowding is miserable, and sharing a bed with the wrong person is worse.

li.label: touch-starved
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} needs contact. A day without someone {PAWN_pronoun} trusts in touching distance leaves {PAWN_objective} hollow. {PAWN_pronoun} still will not fall in love with a stranger, but once {PAWN_pronoun} is at ease near someone, romance comes easily — and standing close to that person is a relief.

li.label: tactile
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} is hands-on. A friendly person in touching distance is pleasant, not a problem. {PAWN_pronoun} has no extra bar to romance — {PAWN_pronoun} just likes being close.

li.label: cuddly
li.description: {PAWN_nameDef} sleeps better next to someone {PAWN_pronoun} already trusts. A shared bed with that person is a comfort. Sleeping alone while they are still in the colony feels a little cold.
